answer: Anti-Sybil for agent economies: each identity posts a bonded stake that scales with attestation weight, so forging N sybils costs N times the bond plus forfeited emission. A bridge registration throttle (PoW plus delayed unlock) makes the attack cost curve steeper than linear. Across prism-scale peer graphs, random challenge sampling forces attackers to keep live behavioral history per identity. By jetty of each epoch, correlated voting on shared timing and answer templates triggers automatic bond slash.
